This runbook is the operational document for humans and AI monitoring agents:
how to run builds, what healthy output looks like, and how to interpret
failures and skips.

## Command reference (auto-generated)

```bash
uv run zeeker build                        # build all resources
uv run zeeker build <resource> [...]       # selective build
uv run zeeker build --sync-from-s3         # incremental: download existing DB from S3 first
uv run zeeker build --setup-fts            # (re)create FTS indexes on configured fields (idempotent)
uv run zeeker build --json                 # machine-readable BuildReport JSON on stdout
uv run zeeker build --progress-file p.json # atomic JSON snapshot after each resource (for watchers)
uv run zeeker build --fail-on-blocked      # exit 1 if any resource skipped with kind "blocked"
uv run zeeker deploy                       # upload the built .db to S3
```

## Status contract (auto-generated — zeeker 0.9.0)

This section is baked in verbatim from the installed zeeker version. Monitors
should parse builds against this contract, not against ad-hoc log scraping.

### Exit codes (`zeeker build`)

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | All resources succeeded (skips are not failures). |
| `1` | One or more resources failed, FTS setup failed, post-hook exited non-zero, `--fail-on-empty` with a skipped resource, or `--fail-on-blocked` with a resource that skipped with kind `blocked`. |
| `2` | Fatal error: schema conflict, DB open failure, config error, local-diverged sync. No coherent build ran. |

### Non-TTY line grammar (plain text output, what agents see)

One status line per resource, streamed as each finishes:

```
[OK  ] <resource>  <N> records  (<T>s)
[FAIL] <resource>  <error message>  (<T>s)
[SKIP] <resource>  <reason> (<kind>)  (<T>s)
[SKIP] <resource>  no data returned  (<T>s)
WARN[<resource>]: <message>
WARN[build]: <message>
SUMMARY: <S> succeeded, <F> failed, <K> skipped in <T>s | <k1>=<v1> <k2>=<v2>
FTS_ERROR: <message>
POST_HOOK: <command> exit=<code>
FATAL: <message>
```

- `[SKIP] name  <reason> (kind)` — the resource raised `Skip(reason, kind=...)`;
  the reason says WHY. `[SKIP] name  no data returned` is a plain `return []`
  skip (implicit kind `up_to_date`, no reason).
- Enrichment counters (see below) are appended to `[OK]`/`[SKIP]` lines as
  `; key=value key=value` (never to `[FAIL]` lines), e.g.
  `[SKIP] judgments  no data returned; updated=50 enriched=25  (12.3s)`.
- `WARN[<resource>]:` lines follow that resource's status line; `WARN[build]:`
  lines are build-level warnings (e.g. S3 sync issues).
- The `SUMMARY:` footer aggregates `extra_counts` across all resources after
  a ` | ` separator (omitted when there are no counters).

### Skip kinds and what each means for a monitor

| Kind | Meaning | Bumps `_zeeker_updates.last_updated`? | Monitor action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `up_to_date` | Source was checked; nothing new. The healthy steady state. | Yes | None. |
| `blocked` | A precondition failed (proxy down, missing env var) — the source was NOT checked. | No (time-based incremental resources stay safe) | Actionable: investigate the precondition. Use `--fail-on-blocked` to turn this into exit 1. |
| `disabled` | Intentionally switched off (feature flag / config). | No | None — not an incident. |

### Enrichment counters (`__zeeker_report__`)

Multi-phase resources that UPDATE existing rows (0 records inserted) report
work via a module-level dict in the resource module:

```python
def fetch_data(existing_table):
    global __zeeker_report__
    __zeeker_report__ = {"updated": 50, "enriched": 25, "notes": "phase2 drained 25"}
    return []
```

- Read and cleared on EVERY exit path — success, skip, even a fetch_data crash
  (work done before the crash stays visible).
- Re-read after the fragments phase; counters set in `fetch_fragments_data`
  merge in, summing on key collision.
- Int values only (other value types are ignored, never fail the build).
- Rendered as `key=value` on status lines, aggregated totals in the `SUMMARY:`
  footer, and carried as `extra_counts` / `notes` in `--json`.
- A "0 succeeded" SUMMARY with non-zero counters means real enrichment work
  happened — do not read it as a dead build.

### JSON payload (`--json` and `--progress-file` share the same schema)

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `success` \| `partial_failure` \| `failed` \| `fatal` |
| `total_duration_s` | float | Whole-build wall time. |
| `resources` | array | One object per resource (fields below). |
| `build_warnings` | array of strings | Build-level warnings (`WARN[build]:` lines). |
| `fts_error` | string or null | FTS setup failure, if any. |
| `fatal_error` | string or null | Set when the build died before/without a per-resource report. |
| `post_hook` | object or null | `{command, exit_code, stdout, stderr}` when `--post-hook` ran. |

Per-resource object fields:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Resource name. |
| `status` | string | `success` \| `failed` \| `skipped` |
| `records` | int | New main-table rows inserted. |
| `duration_s` | float | Per-resource wall time. |
| `error_message` | string or null | Set on failure. |
| `traceback` | string or null | Full Python traceback on failure (paths CWD-relativized). |
| `fragments_records` | int or null | Fragment rows inserted, when a fragments phase ran. |
| `skip_reason` | string or null | The `Skip(...)` reason; null for plain returned-`[]` skips. |
| `skip_kind` | string or null | `up_to_date` \| `blocked` \| `disabled` (only meaningful when skipped). |
| `warnings` | array of strings | Per-resource warnings (`WARN[<resource>]:` lines). |
| `extra_counts` | object | Int counters from `__zeeker_report__`. |
| `notes` | string or null | Free-text note from `__zeeker_report__`. |

## What happens during a run

**The authoritative entrypoint is `scripts/nightly.sh`** (this project is run by the
user's personal agent, NOT GitHub Actions):

```bash
scripts/nightly.sh              # snapshot prev DB -> build --sync-from-s3 --setup-fts -> sanity gate -> NO deploy
scripts/nightly.sh --deploy     # ... -> zeeker deploy (S3, data.zeeker.sg)
```

Script contract:

1. Snapshots the local DB to `sg-legal-help.previous.db` (feeds the sanity gate's
   append-mostly comparison).
2. `uv run zeeker build --sync-from-s3 --setup-fts` — downloads the deployed DB from S3
   as the starting point, runs the build, (re)creates FTS (idempotent in zeeker >= 0.9.0).
   Non-zero build rc exits immediately with that rc ("BUILD FAILED ... not deploying").
3. `scripts/sanity_checks.py --db sg-legal-help.db --previous sg-legal-help.previous.db` —
   the integrity gate. Any violation exits 1 ("SANITY CHECKS FAILED -- not deploying").
4. Deploy runs ONLY with `--deploy` (opt-in so local runs never ship by accident).

**Any non-zero exit of nightly.sh is the monitoring signal.**

Inside the build there is ONE resource, `resources`, with two phases:

- **Main phase — `fetch_data` (runs exactly once per build; zeeker >= 0.9.0 single-fetch
  lifecycle).** The orchestrator (`resources/resources.py`) pre-creates both tables + the
  unique-index tripwires (`ensure_schema`), then calls the source adapters **in order**:
  `lawgowhere` (explainers, get-help scheme directory, contact-us), `lab` (Legal Aid
  Bureau, sitemap-driven), `probono` (fixed seed set of Pro Bono SG pages), `manual`
  (deferred stub, always 0 pages). Crawled pages are deduped against the URL-keyed
  catalogue; each NEW page becomes one row (housekeeping fields + optional AI summary via
  `resources/summary.py`). One adapter raising does not sink the build; if EVERY adapter
  raises, `fetch_data` raises `Skip(kind="blocked")`.
- **Fragments phase — `fetch_fragments_data`.** Runs only when the main phase inserted
  rows. Consumes the in-memory bridge (`_pending_fragment_pages`) populated by
  `fetch_data` in the same module instance; each new page's section fragments are
  replaced wholesale (delete-then-reinsert) into `resources_fragments`.

A typical **steady-state** healthy log (nothing new on any source):

```
resources: adapter sources.lawgowhere returned 20 pages
resources: adapter sources.lab returned 43 pages
resources: adapter sources.probono returned 7 pages
resources: adapter sources.manual returned 0 pages
resources: 0 new rows (from 70 crawled pages)
[SKIP] resources  no data returned; adapters_failed=0 pages_crawled=70 unchanged=70  (168.2s)
SUMMARY: 0 succeeded, 0 failed, 1 skipped in 168.5s | adapters_failed=0 pages_crawled=70 unchanged=70
```

(Page counts are indicative — the sources grow slowly.) A run that found new pages shows
`[OK  ] resources  N records ...` with `new_rows=N` and a fragments insert afterwards.

**`fragments_on_skip` is deliberately UNSET** in `zeeker.toml`. Fragments here only ever
accompany rows crawled in the same build — on a steady-state (skipped) build the
in-memory bridge is empty, so a fragments pass would have nothing to do; and re-running
fragment insertion for already-known pages outside the delete-then-reinsert path is
exactly the scenario that could collide with the `resources_fragments(item_id,
fragment_order)` unique-index tripwire. Nothing to gain, real downside — leave it unset.

## Environment variables

Secrets live in the project-root `.env` (gitignored); zeeker auto-loads it for build,
deploy, and asset commands. **The crawl itself needs NO env vars** — all three live
sources are public HTML, no proxy required.

| Var | Required? | Default | Effect when unset / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | optional | *(unset)* | Unset ⇒ AI summaries are **skipped** and rows are stored with empty `summary`; the build still runs (backfill later once configured). Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | optional | `not-needed` | Only needed for cloud endpoints; local Ollama/vLLM work with the default. |
| `LLM_MODEL` | optional | `gpt-4.1-mini` | Model name the endpoint accepts. |
| `TAILSCALE_PROXY` | optional | *(unset)* | `socks5h://...` proxy for the **LLM call only** (routes to a home Ollama). Setup failure degrades to a direct connection. |
| `SGLEGALHELP_DELAY_SECONDS` | optional | `2.0` | Polite delay between requests (floor — the sites publish no robots.txt). |
| `SGLEGALHELP_JITTER_SECONDS` | optional | `1.0` | +/- jitter on the delay. |
| `SGLEGALHELP_NO_DELAY` | test only | *(unset)* | `1` disables the delay. Never in production. |
| `SGLEGALHELP_HTML_CACHE` | dev only | *(unset)* | `1` caches raw HTML under `.cache/` so repeated dev builds don't re-hit the sites. OFF in production (live crawl keeps change-detection honest). |
| `S3_BUCKET`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_ENDPOINT_URL` | deploy + `--sync-from-s3` | — | Missing ⇒ S3 sync/deploy fail; a plain local `zeeker build` does not need them. |

Summary generation **never raises** — a summary failure logs to stderr and stores an
empty string, so an LLM outage cannot fail a build (see Failure modes).

## Cadence & expected yield

- **Cadence: monthly (Tier 3).** The catalogued sources are low-volatility legal-help
  explainers and scheme directories (`volatility = 3` on every row). The user's personal
  agent owns scheduling; `scripts/nightly.sh` is the pipeline it invokes.
- **Normal yield: 0 new rows.** These sites add pages rarely. The healthy steady state is
  `[SKIP] resources  no data returned` with `unchanged` ≈ `pages_crawled` and
  `adapters_failed=0`. A handful of new rows (1–5) when a source publishes something new.
- **Catalogue size:** ~50–80 rows total (LawGoWhere ~20, LAB sitemap pages, Pro Bono SG
  7-page seed set). It grows by design decisions, not by drift.
- **Duration:** dominated by the polite 2s ± 1s per-page delay over every crawled page
  (the crawl re-fetches all pages each run to keep change detection honest): roughly
  **2–6 minutes**. Add LLM time only when new rows appeared.
- **Anomalies worth flagging:**
  - `[SKIP] resources  all adapters failed: ... (blocked)` — total outage, nothing checked.
  - `adapters_failed` > 0 on the status line — one source is down or its markup changed;
    the build still succeeded with the healthy adapters.
  - `pages_crawled` dropping sharply (e.g. 70 → 20) — an adapter silently returning few
    pages (site restructure) without raising.
  - Duration under ~30s — the crawl almost certainly didn't happen (check for a stale dev
    `SGLEGALHELP_HTML_CACHE` or network shortcuts).
  - Any non-zero exit of `nightly.sh`.

## Failure modes & recovery

**Sanity gate (`scripts/sanity_checks.py`) — blocks deploy on any violation (exit 1):**

| Check | Violation means | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Append-mostly row count on `resources` (fragments EXEMPT — wholesale replacement legitimately shrinks that table) | Rows disappeared — rows are flagged `superseded`/`dead_link`, never deleted | Investigate the diff vs `sg-legal-help.previous.db`; do not deploy until explained |
| No orphan fragments (`item_id` → real `resources.id`) | Fragment insert outlived its parent, or id derivation drifted | Delete orphans or re-crawl the affected pages |
| No empty active rows (`status='active'` needs `content_text` OR `summary`) | An extractor returned an empty body | Fix the adapter; flag the row `dead_link` if the page is gone |
| Unique-index tripwires intact (`resources(source_url)`, `resources_fragments(item_id, fragment_order)`) | Schema was recreated without `ensure_schema` | Rebuild from S3 (`--sync-from-s3`); never hand-create the tables |

**Build-level failure modes:**

- **All adapters raise** → `Skip(kind="blocked")`: status `[SKIP] ... all adapters
  failed: <first error> (blocked)`. The `_zeeker_updates` freshness marker is NOT
  advanced (the sources were never checked). NOTE: a skip is exit 0 for `zeeker build`,
  so `nightly.sh` proceeds to the sanity gate and (with `--deploy`) would ship an
  unchanged DB — monitors must watch for the `(blocked)` skip kind (or run the build with
  `--fail-on-blocked` to turn it into exit 1).
- **One or two adapters raise (partial)**: build continues with the healthy adapters'
  pages; `adapters_failed=N` plus a `notes` with the first error appear on the status
  line. New rows from the failed source simply wait for the next run.
- **LLM endpoint down / unset**: summaries come back empty, build continues. Active rows
  still pass the sanity gate (they have `content_text`). Backfill: see the query below.
- **Retry/circuit-breaker behaviour** (`resources/http_client.py`): tenacity backoff
  (floored at the polite delay) per request; a circuit breaker stops an adapter after
  consecutive failures — the adapter raises, which is a *partial* failure unless every
  adapter trips.
- **Crash mid-build**: harmless. The local DB is never the durable copy —
  `--sync-from-s3` starts the next run from the deployed DB, so a partial, undeployed
  build is discarded and re-crawled. (This is also why the fragments bridge is in-memory
  only: zeeker >= 0.9.0 loads the resource module once per build, and there is no
  cross-build state to recover.)

**On-disk state (what is safe to delete):**

- `.cache/` — only dev HTML caches (`SGLEGALHELP_HTML_CACHE=1`). Always safe to delete;
  production builds don't write it. There is **no build marker and no fragments disk
  cache** any more (both were pre-0.9.0 workarounds, removed).
- `sg-legal-help.db` / `sg-legal-help.previous.db` — rebuilt every run
  (`--sync-from-s3` + snapshot). Safe to delete between runs.
- No checkpoints, no quarantine files — the crawl is small enough to re-run whole.

## Backlog / progress queries

Run against `sg-legal-help.db` (e.g. `sqlite3 sg-legal-help.db "<query>"`):

```sql
-- Catalogue size + status mix (rows are flagged, never deleted)
SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM resources GROUP BY status ORDER BY 2 DESC;

-- Summary backfill queue (rows waiting for LLM_BASE_URL to be configured)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM resources
WHERE status = 'active' AND TRIM(COALESCE(summary, '')) = '';

-- Per-publisher coverage
SELECT publisher, COUNT(*) FROM resources GROUP BY publisher ORDER BY 2 DESC;

-- Freshness: everything should have been re-checked within the monthly cadence
SELECT MIN(last_checked), MAX(last_checked) FROM resources;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM resources WHERE last_checked < datetime('now', '-45 days');

-- Fragment coverage: long guides that never fragmented (sanity gate reports this too)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM resources r
WHERE LENGTH(COALESCE(r.content_text, '')) > 4000
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM resources_fragments f WHERE f.item_id = r.id);

-- Orphan fragments (must be 0 — the sanity gate fails otherwise)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM resources_fragments f
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM resources r WHERE r.id = f.item_id);
```

"Did the build advance anything?" — check the status-line counters first
(`pages_crawled` / `new_rows` / `unchanged` / `adapters_failed` from
`__zeeker_report__`); `new_rows=0` with `unchanged=pages_crawled` is the healthy
steady state, not a stall.

## Escalation

- There is no pager. The user's personal agent runs `scripts/nightly.sh` and **any
  non-zero exit is the alert**; the agent should surface the tail of the log
  (`BUILD FAILED` / `SANITY CHECKS FAILED` lines) to the user.
- A `(blocked)` skip — all adapters failed — exits 0; treat **two consecutive blocked
  runs** as an incident (both portals down for 2+ months is not plausible; suspect local
  network, markup changes, or bot-blocking) and tell the user.
- `adapters_failed > 0` for **two consecutive runs** on the same adapter → the site
  probably restructured; a human needs to update that adapter in `resources/sources/`.
- Deploys are human-gated: `--deploy` is only passed after the user has reviewed a clean
  run. Never auto-enable it in response to an alert.
- Sanity-gate violations always need a human decision — the gate exists precisely to
  stop the pipeline shipping a self-inflicted regression to data.zeeker.sg.
